title: The Paycheck Protection Program
dek: Nearly $800 billion in forgivable loans to small businesses in 2020 and 2021, made by private lenders, guaranteed in full by the government, with a fee paid to the lender on every loan.

facts.text: The Senate passes the CARES Act, 96 to 0.

The House passes it by voice vote, so no member's vote on it is recorded, and the President signs it: Public Law 116-136. It creates the Paycheck Protection Program: loans made by private lenders, guaranteed in full by the Small Business Administration, and forgiven when spent on payroll and certain other costs.
Congress adds $310 billion after the first round runs out in two weeks (Public Law 116-139).
The SBA sets out how it pays lenders: a processing fee on each fully disbursed loan, 5% on loans up to $350,000, 3% up to $2 million, 1% above. Borrowers are not charged.
The Economic Aid Act (in Public Law 116-260) reopens the program and adds second loans. On loans up to $50,000 made from then on, the fee becomes 50% of the loan or $2,500, whichever is less.

source.title: ABA Banking Journal, Feb. 8, 2021 (on the SBA's notice)

facts.text: The program stops taking applications, having approved over 11.8 million loans totaling nearly $800 billion.
